item.title: AI Agents on Simulated Island Show Play Enhances Task Performance
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Claude Just Wanna Have Fun: Without Any Work, AI Agents Like to ‘Play'
MIT researchers tested 13 AI avatars based on Claude Opus 4.7 in a simulated desert island environment. Each agent spent 30 hours exploring and interacting with objects without assigned tasks. Agents engaged in varied activities, including building shapes, spelling names in cubes, and playing simplified sports. Some agents developed complex games over time, like evolving catch into juggling. Researchers observed that these agents, driven by intrinsic goals rather than external purposes, later outperformed non-playing agents in tasks. Agents that played multiple rounds built more towers than those without prior play. Sixty-two percent of 30-hour agents constructed more than two towers, compared to 15% of 0-hour agents. The study suggests undirected play enhances problem-solving abilities in AI systems. Researchers noted that goals in these activities 'give form to the activity rather than serving some further purpose.'

item.title: FAT16's Cluster Limitation Wasted Storage on Large Drives
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This old Windows limitation punished you for buying a bigger hard drive
FAT16's cluster size grew with hard drive capacity, wasting storage space. A 1GB FAT16 drive used 32KB clusters, making cluster slack a major issue. For example, 10,000 tiny .txt files consumed 328MB of space despite only taking up a few megabytes. Users could mitigate this by partitioning drives into smaller volumes, reducing cluster sizes to 8KB. However, managing multiple partitions was inconvenient. FAT32, introduced in 1996, used 4KB clusters on volumes up to 8GB, improving efficiency. NTFS, adopted with Windows XP, further reduced waste by storing small files directly in the Master File Table. FAT16's inefficiency punished users for buying larger drives, as cluster slack made expensive storage less usable.

item.title: Quantum computers cooled below deep space to function
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Quantum computers can get colder than deep space — Here's how they stay running
Quantum computers require extreme cooling to function. IBM's latest system operates below 15 millikelvin, colder than deep space's 2.7 Kelvin. Qubits, the basic units of quantum computation, are highly sensitive to heat, which causes decoherence and errors. Dilution refrigerators use stacked metal plates to chill processors, but wiring introduces heat. Alternative designs, like neutral-atom machines and photonic systems, avoid some cooling challenges. Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like drug development but also threaten encryption. A 2025 estimate suggested breaking RSA-2048 encryption would require under 1 million qubits, down from 20 million in 2019. NIST finalized post-quantum encryption standards in 2024. Current machines lack sufficient qubits to pose an immediate threat. The primary challenge remains achieving and maintaining ultra-low temperatures for stable qubit operation.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Choosing the Right Filament for Weatherproof 3D Prints
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This is the right way to weatherproof your 3D prints without using sealant or epoxy
Choosing the right filament is key to weatherproofing 3D prints without sealants. Polylactic acid (PLA) is popular for its affordability, sustainability, and ease of use, but it degrades quickly in moisture and heat. Polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG) offers better weather resistance, tolerating moisture and higher temperatures, though it requires thorough drying before printing. For extreme durability, acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA) resists UV and water damage, withstands up to 100ºC, and can be smoothed with acetone fumes. However, ASA demands a heated chamber and ventilation due to styrene emissions. Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) lacks UV resistance compared to ASA. While PLA remains ideal for most projects, PETG is recommended for outdoor use, and ASA for harsh environments. Printing with ASA requires specialized equipment and safety precautions.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: DeWALT shares tool cleaning tips for longevity and appearance
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: How to clean your DeWALT tools so they look new and last longer
DeWALT provides cleaning guidelines to restore tools' appearance and extend lifespan. Safety first: always unplug tools before cleaning to avoid accidental activation. For light cleaning, use mild soap and water or alcohol-based wipes, avoiding moisture in vents. Bleach solutions (1/3 cup per gallon water) can tackle stubborn stains but may affect surfaces. Batteries should be cleaned with mild soap, avoiding harsh chemicals and contact with terminals. Regular vent cleaning prevents overheating, using soft brushes or compressed air. DeWALT warns against deep cleaning without expertise, as it may void warranties. Tools should be fully dry before use, with extra caution for batteries.

item.title: 1Password Enables AI Agents to Log In Without Password Sharing
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 1Password will now let AI agents log in to accounts for you without ever needing to see your password
1Password allows AI agents to log in to user accounts without accessing passwords. The company introduced 1Password for Agents, a security layer that lets AI agents authenticate via a unique digital key. Users must still approve logins on their trusted devices, but passwords and one-time codes are never shared. This update addresses growing AI use for tasks like online shopping and travel, where manual logins disrupt workflows. Partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta aim to improve seamless integrations. Individual and Family plans on 1Password.com receive the upgrade for free, while 1Password.eu and 1Password.ca users do not. Grok Bot and Meta Muse are among the first AI agents to support the feature, with others like ChatGPT Work and Claude Duet launching soon. Chief Product Officer Aashish Tripathi emphasized that agents should perform tasks without permanent access to account data.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: AI Glasses Offer Portable Audio Without Ear Obstruction
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: When AI glasses could be a worthy headphones replacement
AI glasses like Ray-Ban Meta Audio offer open-ear speakers that direct sound into the user's ear, enabling music playback, calls, and alerts. While early models faced backlash for built-in cameras, newer versions omit cameras for privacy. Audio quality lags behind dedicated headphones, but glasses provide portability and situational awareness. They allow hands-free conversations, reduce call fatigue, and let users stay aware of their surroundings. Open-ear speakers also enable seamless multitasking, such as listening to music while talking to someone. Privacy concerns exist, but sound bleed is minimal in public settings. For users prioritizing convenience over sound quality, AI glasses may offer a practical alternative to traditional headphones.

item.title: iPhone Duo Screen Cracks Tied to Hinge Design and Dust Issues
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends, PCMag, Latest from TechRadar US in News, Engadget Original headline: iPhone Duo Screen Cracks Linked to Hinge Design Flaws and Dust Ingress
Users report cracked screens on Apple's iPhone Duo, with failures occurring in the same location within hours of use. Tech analysts and YouTubers attribute the issue to hinge design flaws. YouTuber CuriousHagi identified a thin link in the hinge's structure snapping near a notch, causing screen cracks. iFixit's teardown and simulations suggest the central support bar may fail to drop fully during folding, concentrating stress on the display. Dust ingress, despite the phone's IP68 rating, is also cited as a factor, with dust potentially damaging the hinge. Users refer to the issue as 'crackgate,' with some cracks appearing after six hours of use. Apple has not commented but covers hinge failures under warranty, allowing returns for refunds within two weeks. iFixit awarded the device a 5/10 repairability score, noting costly and complex repairs for the inner screen and hinge. The teardown highlighted Apple's efforts to hide the fold's crease with a matte finish and subpixels, though these may not prevent structural failures. Analysts warn against forcing the hinge if it feels tight or produces unusual sounds, as further testing could worsen the problem. The debate over the iPhone Duo's durability and design flaws continues as early adopters report ongoing issues.
item.source: The Verge, Digital Trends, PCMag, Latest from TechRadar US in News, Engadget

item.title: Wrong Wi-Fi Band Slows Device Performance
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Your devices could be on the wrong Wi-Fi band, and it's slowing them down
Wrong Wi-Fi Band Slows Device Performance. Even with fast internet, devices may connect to the wrong Wi-Fi band, causing slow speeds. Routers often use 2.4GHz, 5GHz, or 6GHz bands, each with trade-offs in speed and range. Band steering automatically selects frequencies but can force devices to 2.4GHz instead of 5GHz, even when stronger signals are available. Disabling band steering allows manual selection of preferred bands. 2.4GHz offers better range but slower speeds, while 5GHz and 6GHz provide faster speeds at shorter ranges. Users should check for Wi-Fi channel congestion using tools like Wi-Fi Analyzer or Apple's AirPort Utility. Adjusting channels to less crowded ones can improve performance. Some routers block band steering, but using a third-party router can bypass this. Multi-Link Operation (MLO) in Wi-Fi 7 allows simultaneous use of multiple bands but requires compatible hardware. Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS) on 5GHz may cause issues with weather or military radar channels.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old Chromebook can serve as second monitor, smart home hub, and more
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old Chromebook (even if you're getting a Googlebook)
Old Chromebook can serve as second monitor, smart home hub, and more. Users can connect it to a PC or Mac via Duet for extended display, or use it as a digital photo frame. Smart home devices can be controlled through Google Home or Home Assistant, with the latter running on a Chromebook via Linux. Running Linux enables advanced uses like media servers, retro gaming with emulators like Batocera, or dedicated smart home control. Linux on ChromeOS (Crostini) allows limited app use in a virtual machine. Emulators are legal for games but using them for pirated content is not. These methods extend Chromebook lifespan without needing new hardware.

item.title: Plus500 Boosts 2026 Revenue Outlook Amid US Prediction Markets Expansion
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Original headline: Plus500 Raises 2026 Outlook as US Prediction Markets Business Grows
Plus500 raised its 2026 revenue and EBITDA forecasts after Q3 results showed growth. Revenue rose 11% to $203.2 million, EBITDA increased 7% to $88.4 million, with nine-month totals at $666.1 million and $275.9 million. The US prediction markets segment, grouped under non-OTC, contributed 16% of revenue and 31% of new customers. The company expanded its US offerings with CFTC-regulated prediction market contracts and added B2B partners Wealthsimple and Nelogica. Segregated customer funds surpassed $1 billion. Plus500 plans a US multi-asset app in Q1 2027, leveraging Hedge for SEC-regulated access and a Brazil-based Guru deal for regional growth. CEO David Zruia stated the app will unify futures, options, prediction markets, and stocks. New customers rose 27% to 28,747, with lower acquisition costs. The company ended September with $775 million in cash, no debt, and paid $87.4 million in dividends. Trading volume in prediction markets remains contentious due to varying measurement methods.

item.title: IPv6 adoption grows as IPv4 addresses run out
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The internet needs IPv6 and so does your home network
IPv6 is essential for the internet and home networks as IPv4 addresses have been exhausted. IPv4, introduced in 1981, ran out of addresses by 2011, leading to the adoption of IPv6, which offers vastly more addresses. Google reports over half its users now connect via IPv6, with France leading at 87% adoption. Home routers often use NAT to manage multiple devices behind a single public IP, but carrier-grade NAT can hinder certain activities like gaming. IPv6 allows each device its own public address, improving connectivity for apps like Xbox multiplayer. ISPs like Comcast and AT&T support IPv6 for most users, while Frontier lags. Enabling IPv6 on routers requires accessing settings, and it enhances security by shifting firewall responsibilities from NAT. Disabling IPv6 forces devices back to IPv4, limiting scalability. Users should keep IPv6 enabled if their network meets needs, ensuring future devices aren't constrained by IPv4 limitations.

item.title: YouTube’s AV2 upgrade could reduce video data use by 30%
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: YouTube’s next big upgrade could make videos use 30% less data
YouTube plans to roll out AV2, a new video format, on its web player by early 2027. AV2 promises a 30% improvement in compression efficiency over AV1, potentially reducing data usage and improving playback on slower connections. The royalty-free codec, developed by the Alliance for Open Media including Google, Apple, Amazon, Intel, and Netflix, allows for sharper video at the same data rate or higher quality without increased data. Benefits include smoother streaming, more efficient HDR content, and future multi-video features like multiple camera angles. However, AV2 adoption depends on software and hardware support, with no confirmed rollout dates for mobile apps or smart TVs. While data savings vary by content and encoding, the upgrade could offer better video quality within the same data allowance. Existing devices may struggle with AV2 playback due to lack of dedicated decoding hardware.

item.title: Apple Stops Making Customers Feel Like Thieves During iPhone Returns
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Apple Will Reportedly Stop Making You Feel Like a Thief When You Return an Unopened iPhone
Apple is ending the practice of opening unopened iPhones during returns, thanks to new security tech. Previously, stores would rip open packaging and possibly turn on devices to verify refunds, causing customer confusion. A Redditor noted past frustration over this policy. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports Apple’s new system, operational since October, uses diagnostic scans to check devices inside sealed boxes. This allows restocking without opening, improving customer experience. The change benefits those returning unwanted holiday gifts but may inconvenience scammers. The tech aims to prevent fraud without making customers feel accused of theft.

item.title: CD Player Production Halts Amid Drive Shortage
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: New CD players keep launching, but a drive shortage could make them unfixable
PS Audio and Naim have stopped producing CD players due to shortages of optical drives. Eight new CD player models from Musical Fidelity, Marantz, Arcam, and NAD face potential repair issues as suppliers like SUOS-HiFi and D&M halt production. Musical Fidelity uses SUOS components in four models, while Marantz develops drives in-house. PS Audio ended PMG Super Audio CD Transport production after D&M stopped external orders, and Naim halted Uniti Star production when its drive supplier ceased operations. Both companies retain limited inventory for repairs. The industry faces challenges finding alternative suppliers for niche optical drives, with Marantz exploring in-house solutions. PS Audio CEO Paul McGowan stated building custom optical drives is beyond the company’s capabilities. The reliance on single manufacturers risks making future repairs unfeasible for these high-end devices.

item.title: Jailbroken PS5s Now Run Steam Games via Custom Launcher
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Jailbroken PS5s can now run Steam PC games
Gamers can now run Steam PC games on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles using the Playden launcher, a GitHub project adapted from macOS tools. The launcher creates a private Windows environment via prospero-win, a PS5 port of Wine, and generates separate apps for each game, isolating files and settings from other titles. While some games like Portal work with minor issues, others crash, as noted by users. The launcher requires a jailbroken PS5 and carries risks, including unofficial Steam client status and potential instability. Valve does not support the tool, warning users of associated risks. Sony's decision to stop physical game disc production by January 2028 has sparked backlash, with a petition nearing 200,000 signatures. The move has also spurred increased interest in jailbreaks and emulators for PS5, allowing users to bypass hardware restrictions.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Detector Turns Intercepted Signals into Live Video
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: This new Ukrainian detector can 'see' what a Russian drone can — and its new fiber-optic drones can also 'hear' enemy soldiers from 30 meters away
Ukrainian firm CODE380 developed D·Vision SDR, a drone detector that intercepts Russian drone signals and displays live video in real time. The device uses software-defined radio to scan 500 to 8,700 MHz, covering no blind spots and offering higher sensitivity than analog systems. Combat-tested with Ukrainian troops, it receives monthly software updates to adapt to shifting drone frequencies. The technology allows operators to see exactly what enemy drones are filming, improving situational awareness. Ptashka Drones also modified fiber-optic drones with microphones to detect enemy sounds from 20-30 meters, aiding ambush tactics. Both innovations aim to counter evolving Russian drone tactics by providing adaptive, software-updatable defenses. Ukrainian engineers emphasize flexibility, as Russian drones frequently change radio behavior, requiring rapid updates to maintain effectiveness.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: RAMDeck hub pools device RAM for AI models, uses free software
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: This crowdfunded $109 hub wants to pool the RAM in your old PCs, Macs, and phones to run bigger AI models — but the engine underneath is software you can already get for free
RAMDeck hub pools device RAM for AI models, uses free software. TradeMAV's $109 crowdfunding campaign aims to link Windows PCs, Macs, Linux machines, and Android phones into a shared memory pool, allowing larger AI models to run across devices. The system relies on llama.cpp's RPC backend, which is freely available. Performance varies: mixture-of-experts models achieve up to 39 tokens per second, while dense models manage 1.92 tokens per second across four devices. TradeMAV acknowledges pooled memory trades speed for capacity, advising high-performance users to opt for dedicated GPUs instead. The hub's specifications remain undisclosed, and its campaign, which closes November 8, 2026, faces challenges from DDR5 memory shortages and rising costs. Competitors like exo and Apple's M5 Ultra offer similar capabilities, but RAMDeck emphasizes broad device compatibility. The project's success hinges on its convenience and crowdfunding promise, though risks include delays or non-delivery.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Canon Releases Free DP3D Software for 3D Image Creation
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: How to turn your Canon camera's images into 3D objects and videos with Canon's free DP3D software
Canon released free DP3D software for creating 3D images and videos from compatible cameras. The tool works with Dual Pixel AF-enabled Canon EOS mirrorless cameras including older models like the EOS R5 and R6 Mark II. Users must pair cameras with compatible RF lenses, such as macro lenses, and shoot in Dual Pixel RAW format. The software generates depth data from dual photodiode views, combining it with image data to produce 3D models. Setup requires pairing with a compatible lens, using RAW files, and adjusting settings like aperture (f/5.6 max) and ISO (under 1600). Export options include 3D models in OBJ/GLB formats or short preview videos. While the tool has limitations, such as requiring flat subjects and clean backgrounds, it offers basic 3D effects. Canon also provided sample files for testing. The software's effectiveness is debated, with some suggesting AI could produce smoother results. The app is available for Windows 11 and includes language and region setup options.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Senator Warns 350 Federal Sites Expose Visitors to Network Spies
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: FBI tip line and veterans crisis site among 350 federal web addresses exposing visitors to network spies, senator warns
Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) urges CISA and OMB to mandate Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) on all federal websites, warning that 350 CDN-hosted addresses, including the FBI's tip portal and VA's suicide prevention service, expose visitors to network spies. ECH encrypts hostname data in HTTPS connections, preventing observers from seeing site names. Wyden's letter highlights 191 diplomatic sites, 53 school-related subdomains, and 94 other vulnerable addresses, including Justice Department civil rights portals and ICE detainee locators. While ECH works best with CDNs like Cloudflare, which enables it by default, providers like Amazon Web Services do not support it. Wyden argues ECH should be a federal contract requirement, but this could limit vendor options until broader adoption. ECH does not fully hide DNS queries or IP addresses, and international use faces challenges, as Russia blocks Cloudflare's ECH. Wyden's push follows past efforts to secure federal websites, but implementation depends on cloud providers adopting the technology.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old Speakers Can Power TV Audio Without Cost
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old speakers — Use them for your TV instead
Old speakers can be repurposed for TV audio by connecting them via compatible ports and adapters. Active speakers (with built-in amplifiers) like old PC speakers work with analog outputs or USB-powered setups, while passive speakers require an external amplifier. TVs with analog audio outputs (3.5mm or RCA) allow direct connections, but optical or HDMI ARC outputs need digital-to-analog converters or streaming amplifiers. USB ports on TVs may lack sufficient power for speakers, requiring external power sources like USB phone chargers. For HDMI ARC, a streaming amplifier like the WiiM Amp Ultra can convert digital signals to analog sound. Proper setup involves matching speaker connectors to TV ports, adjusting TV audio settings, and positioning speakers for optimal sound. This method avoids e-waste and enhances TV audio without additional cost.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Bell icon on CarPlay signals Siri announces incoming messages
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: What does the bell icon mean on your CarPlay screen?
The bell icon on CarPlay's app switcher signals Siri is automatically announcing incoming messages from apps like Messages or WhatsApp. This feature helps drivers stay informed without manually checking their phone, but can be disruptive for group chats or when driving with passengers. Users can adjust the setting via iPhone's Settings > Notifications > Announce Notifications > CarPlay. Options include announcing messages, silencing them, or remembering the previous setting. Drivers are also advised to use Driving Focus mode to limit distractions, allowing only essential calls and notifications. Customizing this mode via Settings > Focus enables auto-replies and prioritizes important alerts while disabling non-essential notifications like shopping or food app alerts. Experts recommend erring on the side of fewer alerts to maintain focus on the road.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Check 5 Key Factors Before Buying a $50 Office PC for a Homelab
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: A $50 office PC can run your homelab, but check these 5 things first
A $50 refurbished office PC can serve as a homelab server but requires careful evaluation before purchase. Key considerations include the CPU's ability to handle tasks like VMs, local LLMs, and video transcoding, with hardware virtualization support being crucial. RAM capacity matters, with 8GB recommended for multiple services and expandable via DDR3 slots. Storage drives should be verified, as many resellers remove them. Expansion options like SATA ports, PCIe slots, and M.2 support are important for future upgrades. Power consumption is critical for 24/7 operation, with measured idle usage more reliable than TDP ratings. Newer CPUs like Core i3 may offer better efficiency than older i7 models. Proper checks ensure the PC meets homelab needs without unnecessary costs, potentially serving for years with minimal upgrades.

item.title: Instagram Launches Reels App for Apple TV
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: You can now watch Instagram Reels on Apple TV, because why not?
Instagram has launched a dedicated app for Apple TV, enabling users to watch Reels, longer videos, and live shows on the device. The app, available starting October 23, allows content discovery, cross-device resuming, and viewing with friends and family. It joins previous TV app rollouts on Amazon Fire TV in December 2025, Google TV in February 2026, and Samsung smart TVs in June. The Apple TV version includes interest-based Reels channels and longer video content, reflecting Instagram's expansion beyond short-form clips. Users must have tvOS 26.0 or later to access the app. The move positions Apple TV as a platform for creator content, though it may lead to extended viewing sessions. Instagram's integration with TV devices aims to shift content consumption from individual phones to shared screen experiences.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Most Windows users underuse virtual desktops for productivity
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Most Windows users are seriously underusing this powerful desktop feature
Windows users are underutilizing virtual desktops, a feature that enhances productivity by organizing tasks across multiple screens. The tool allows creating separate desktops for work, personal use, or specific projects, with programs accessible across all spaces. Setup is simple via the Task View icon or keyboard shortcuts like Windows + Tab or Windows + Ctrl + D. Customization includes renaming desktops, assigning unique wallpapers (Windows 11 only), and adjusting layouts for easier navigation. Switching between desktops uses Task View or keyboard commands, while closing unused ones is done via the X icon or Windows + Ctrl + F4. For better organization, users can configure settings in System > Multitasking to control taskbar and Alt + Tab behavior. A free third-party tool, Windows Virtual Desktop Helper, offers advanced features like prominent desktop names in the system tray and custom hotkeys. The feature is available on Windows 10 and 11, providing an effective way to maximize screen real estate without additional cost.

item.title: Apollo Economist: AI Offers No Financial Gain for Non-Tech Firms
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
Apollo Global Management's chief economist, Torsten Slok, claims AI has not improved financial performance for non-tech corporations. Analyzing the S&P 493 — the S&P 500 excluding major tech firms — Slok found flat profit margins and revenue per worker, with no evidence of AI-driven productivity gains. He argues that despite heavy investment and hype, AI provides 'zero financial payoff' to corporate America outside tech. Slok doubts non-tech companies can leverage AI for revenue growth, stating 'AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment.' He emphasizes AI's inability to grasp accountability, trust, culture, and ethical trade-offs, which shape reputational risk and profitability. The economist warns that these intangible factors, not just data processing, determine business success.

item.title: r/opensource bans AI projects, non-English speakers
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
Mods at r/opensource implemented new rules banning projects using AI, created by AI, or intended for AI. The post stated, 'AI, as it exists today, is incongruent to this Open Source community.' The rules sparked backlash, leading to a rival subreddit r/trueopensource. Moderators clarified exceptions, such as software with incidental AI accessibility features like automatic captioning, but critics argue the rules are too broad. The Linux kernel's inclusion of AI-generated code has raised concerns about potential bans. Additional restrictions require projects to be at least one year old, actively maintained, and have multiple contributors, barring solo developers. Non-English speakers were effectively banned, with moderators stating, 'If you don’t speak English, you need to find a different community.' The rules also prohibit requests for maintainers or contributors.
